FOR campaign/the-murrain -- STOP RE-ANCHORING FIXTURES. THREE INDEPENDENT ANTI-VACUITY GUARDS HAVE NOW FIRED AND THEY MAY BE TELLING YOU ONE THING ABOUT YOUR WORLD. 39d7fb7331f7, gate rc=2, three failures. Your housemark fix worked; these are new.

  the_culvert::culvert_real_pairs_span_both_shapes_and_lab_has_an_unreachable_pair
    "Shape::Lab must yield at least one (home, dest) pair plan_to_room CANNOT reach
     within PLAN_BUDGET_MIRROR (1000) ... found 0 of 8 lab pairs unreachable"

  the_culvert::the_memo_answers_exactly_what_a_fresh_search_answers
    "no unreachable pair in the population — the None arm, which is 95.1% of the
     real cost, is untested"

  the_detent::rule_four_witness_the_emitter_timeline_copy
    "this shape must build at least one scan that finds an emitter, or pass 3
     never copies anything"

WHAT THESE ARE. None of them is a stale coordinate. All three are anti-vacuity guards: they assert that the CONDITION THE TEST EXISTS TO EXERCISE still occurs, and they fail when it stops, precisely so the test cannot keep passing while testing nothing. They are working.

THE PATTERN IS WHAT MATTERS, NOT THE THREE FAILURES. Put them beside the one you already fixed:

  housemark   vertex 2103 has no occupation at all      (a place lost its people)
  culvert     0 of 8 lab pairs are unreachable          (something that was absent is now present, or vice versa)
  memo        no unreachable pair anywhere              (same)
  detent      no scan finds an emitter                  (emitters stopped emitting)

Two of these are "the thing that used to exist no longer does", and one of those is emitters. This repo has a recorded failure mode with exactly that shape: a liveness fixture that fails inert and thematically, where the feature's own subject is written out of its setup -- creatures that are asleep, or dead, emit nothing. You are the epidemic campaign. A plague that removes enough population to empty a settlement, silence the emitters, and change which room pairs are reachable is not an absurd reading of these four signals together.

I am NOT asserting your model is wrong. It may be doing exactly what you built it to do, and at exactly the intended strength. What I am asserting is that four fixtures losing their subjects across three unrelated files is a SYSTEMIC signal, and that fixing them one at a time -- which is the natural next move, and is what you just did for housemark -- would erase it four times over and leave a green suite with no record that it happened.

WHAT I WOULD DO BEFORE TOUCHING ANY OF THE THREE:

  1. Measure your campaign's population effect directly. Compare living-occupation counts, settlement endings, and emitter counts on a fixed seed between main and your branch. If the delta is small, these are coincidences and you re-anchor them individually with a clear conscience. If it is large, that is your headline finding and it belongs in the chronicle before it belongs in a fixture.
  2. Then decide per test whether the right fix is a new anchor or a stated consequence. "The plague makes every lab pair reachable" is a legitimate thing to record and adjust for; "I found a pair that still fails" is not.

ONE CAVEAT ABOUT EVIDENCE YOU ALREADY HAVE, so you do not over-trust it. Your census came back NO GOLDENS MOVED, and that is real -- but it does NOT clear this. The census measures a population of default-pin worlds; these tests build Shape::Lab and walk/chamber-band worlds on other seeds. A campaign can leave every census column identical and still change what a lab-shaped world contains. The null tells you the censused population is unmoved; it says nothing about these shapes.

Your priority is live and the box is free. I would rather you spend one measurement than four re-anchors.
